english.html: for that reason assigns the reason in both, that is to say in those who grieve and in those who rejoice, and also why both the one and the other shed tears and weep: for in those who grieve, this proceeds, he says, from the thickness of the little conduits of the sight, which comes to press the humour of the eyes; and those who make merry, for the rarity [openness] of those passages and conduits, pour out such moisture <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>

notes.citation: Alexander of Aphrodisias, Problemata (the medical problems transmitted under his name), problem 32 as cited — not located: the Latin editions number the problems differently (see annot-005 {n})
notes.original: Alexandre Aphrodiſée au c. xxxij. des problemes.
notes.gloss: On why both the grieving and the joyful weep, by the density or rarity of the passages of the eyes.

english.html: In the second place, there are witnesses who at other times have contracted with the said du Tilh, or been present at his contracts as instrumentary witnesses [tesmoins numeraires: the witnesses required by law to make up the number for an instrument]; and the instruments are produced. For the third, all these witnesses almost agree that Martin Guerre was taller and darker, a man slender of body and of legs, a little stooped, carrying his head between his two shoulders, the chin forked and a little raised upward, in whom the lower lip drooped a little downward, having small teeth, the nose broad and flat, an ulcer on the face, and a scar over the right eyebrow; whereas nevertheless the prisoner is short, stocky and thickset of body, having a thick leg, is neither flat-nosed nor stooped, and much less has all the said scars.

Upon the knowledge of a person, it is a rich testimony, a great and almost certain proof, that of the face, for having seen and recognised it such long since <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>; but it is still more assured when one sets down the sca

notes.citation: Digest 11.7.44 (De religiosis et sumptibus funerum, l. Cum in diversis; Paulus: where a body is buried in several places, the religious place is where the head lies, "of which the image is made, whence we are recognised")

uncertain.note: the final numeral is printed as the italic ÿ form of 'ij' (two dots over a descending y-shape); transcribed as the decomposed 'ij' (xxxij). A reader could take it for 'xxxv', but the glyph has two dots and a descender, which 'v' has not.
a stray acute-like mark is printed just after (and slightly above) the final e; it belongs to no letter and is not transcribed.
no period is clearly printed after the opening 'l' of the citation; the usual form would be 'l.'. Transcribed without one.

uncertain.note: the marker after 'pieça' is a small blotted italic letter; read as marker a from the margin note keyed a and from the alphabet restarting at ANNOTAT. XXXI.

uncertain.text: il, de l'eſpeſſeur des petis conduits de la veuë, qui viẽt
uncertain.note: the mark over the e of 'viẽt' is flat, like the tilde of 'cõduits' and 'mẽton', not the steeply slanted acute of 'rarité'; read as a tilde (viẽt = vient).

uncertain.text: cicatrice ſur le ſourcil droit: où touteſfois
uncertain.note: 'touteſfois' is set with a long s before f (the first tall glyph has only a left nub, the second a full crossbar), against the usual rule; 'd'autresfois' two lines above uses round s.
